topic: What happens if an avalanche buries you?
title: Buried By An Avalanche
idea: Snow sets like concrete and the clock decides who lives; three things you do yourself before it sets.
hook: You just got buried by an avalanche.

beats.line: The snow stops, and it sets around you like concrete.
You can't move. You can't even tell which way is up.
Your warm breath melts the snow at your face, then it freezes into a mask of ice.
Dug out within fifteen minutes, nine in ten people survive.
After thirty five minutes, it's only about three.
So rewind. Before the snow sets, remember three things.
One. Get your hands in front of your mouth. That's your air pocket.
Two. Don't spit to find which way is up. It's a myth. You can't dig out anyway.
Three. Punch a hand up, so they can find you.

end.line: Save this. You won't have time to look it up.

description: Buried by an avalanche: the snow sets like concrete. Three things to remember before it does.

facts.claim: Avalanche debris sets hard once it stops ('like you are buried in concrete'); you cannot dig yourself out and may not know which way is up.
facts.source: Mt. Shasta Avalanche Center, FAQ (shastaavalanche.org/page/faq); University of Utah Health, Three winter wilderness survival myths, 2022

facts.claim: Exhaled moisture freezes into a thin mask of ice in front of the face that impairs air exchange.
facts.source: JAMA 1994 (air-pocket device paper, jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/articlepdf/192660/jpc00001.pdf) - videne len v uryvku, nie cely text

facts.claim: About 9 in 10 survive when dug out within 15 minutes (92 % Falk 1994; 90.6 % for 0-15 min in Swiss data 1981-2020). Newest framing: steep drop already after 10 minutes.
facts.source: Falk, Brugger, Adler-Kastner, Nature 1994; Rauch et al., JAMA Network Open 2024
Falk et al., Nature 1994 (cit. v Rauch 2024)

facts.claim: Clear an air space in front of your mouth before the snow sets; even a small pocket prolongs survival.
facts.source: Mt. Shasta Avalanche Center, FAQ (shastaavalanche.org/page/faq); University of Utah Health, Three winter wilderness survival myths, 2022

facts.claim: Spitting to find which way is up is a myth: it does not matter, you cannot dig out of debris.
facts.source: Mt. Shasta Avalanche Center, FAQ (shastaavalanche.org/page/faq); University of Utah Health, Three winter wilderness survival myths, 2022

facts.claim: Push a hand upward: a visible clue lets companions find you faster.

factcheck.note: Krok 2 'Spit' bol mytus (Shasta, Utah Health) -> zmenene na vyvratenie mytu. 'fewer than three' -> 'about three' (Falk 30 %). 'Cup your hands' -> 'hands in front of your mouth'.
